I have farmed these 7.5 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I never went to school, cannot read the words on the fertilizer bags, but I know every corner of my land. My wife and I are the only ones at home — our children work in Handan and send a little money, but I do not ask them for farm money. This is my responsibility.

I keep 4 mu on the south side for cotton. That is my main crop, what I know best. I buy improved cotton seed from the county store every year — about 2.5 jin per mu. Before planting in late April, I run the rotary tiller and spread compound fertilizer, about one big bag for every two mu. Cotton needs a lot of spraying. I spray for bollworm about twelve times through the summer, and once for weeds. If you skip even one spray and the worms come, the bolls drop and you lose everything. I irrigate three times from the well — at flowering, at boll-setting, and once more in August if the weather turns dry. Pumping costs electricity, but cotton pays better than grain when the price is right, so I do not skip water.

The other 3.5 mu I do wheat and corn, one after the other. I plant winter wheat in mid-October, right after the corn comes off. I use the same improved wheat seed I have been buying for years. I put compound fertilizer down before planting, about one bag per two mu, and then in March when the wheat turns green, if it looks yellow I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. I irrigate wheat three times because it is our safety crop — even if cotton fails, we have grain. I spray herbicide once in early spring. Corn goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The window is so tight, sometimes only two days, so I use hybrid seed and put all the fertilizer in the furrow at planting. No time for topdressing. I do a quick no-till planting if the ground is soft, or one pass with the rotary tiller if the stubble is thick. I irrigate corn twice if the summer is dry, but usually the rains help. One spray for weeds and one for insects is enough.

I do not hire labor. It costs at least 150 yuan a day now, and with just my wife and me we manage. Old Wang down the road has a rotary tiller, and we trade favors. At 60, I do not try new things anymore. Change is just risk. I expect about 900 jin per mu of cotton seed, 800 jin per mu of wheat, and 900 jin per mu of corn if the weather holds. Last year was decent. I hope this year is the same.
